run.rulesInOwnWords:
Starting position: six segments, numbered 1 (bottom) to 6 (top), all QUIET. Capacities are 10 8 12 6 9 7, upper marks 7 6 9 5 7 5, lower marks 3 2 4 2 3 2. Starting sap is 3 6 6 2 2 1 (total 20). Each cycle runs five steps in a fixed order, and each step is applied to all six segments before the next step begins.
Step 1, Feed: add that cycle's feed row to each segment. Do not check capacity.
Step 2, Push: go through segments 1 to 6 in order. If a segment holds more than its capacity, cut it back to capacity and add the excess to the next segment up before checking that one. So a surge can carry through several segments. Any excess from segment 6 is lost (transpired).
Step 3, Marks: a QUIET segment whose sap is at or above its upper mark becomes SINK-ACTIVE. A SINK-ACTIVE segment at or below its lower mark becomes QUIET. Otherwise the state stays the same. Every flip is logged.
Step 4, Draw down: first work out every amount from the sap each segment holds after step 3. A QUIET segment loses floor(sap/4), which is lost (respired). A SINK-ACTIVE segment sends floor(sap/2) to the segment below. Segment 1's send leaves the books and counts as loss. All moves happen at once. Capacity is not checked.
Step 5, Leaf-drop (the global reset): if the stem total is strictly more than 38, every segment becomes floor(sap/2). The amount removed (sap minus floor(sap/2)) is lost (transpired).
Loss tally = transpired + respired + sent past segment 1, starting from 0. Balance check: start + total fed = amount standing at the end + loss tally.

gapsFlagged.whatYouAssumed: 'Halve, rounding down' means the amount kept is floor(sap/2). The amount removed is therefore the larger half, ceil(sap/2), and it is transpired.
The total checked against 38 is the stem total after the step 4 draw-down in that same cycle.
Draw-down uses the states as they stand after step 3 of the same cycle, including any flips just made.
Draw-down can leave a segment over capacity. It stays that way into the next cycle's feed and push, and stays that way at the final report. This case never came up in this run.
